PC: Quick management: upright position, O2, NTG, MSO4, lasix, consider inotropes? (dobutamine, dopamine, PDI (milrinone); note learning point: when to use or avoid betablockers & ACEI for acute decompensated CHF
Quick orders: EKG(LVH,atrial dil, LBBB, old MI), CXR, BNP, CE, chem7, ABG, CBC
On a separate handout, individual learners are asked to provide medication orders, fluid orders (if appropriate), follow-up labs and tests (15 min).
MK: Etiology of acute CHF—MI, infxn, anemia etc
SBP: Identify required level of care by obtaining appropriate information using history, physical exam findings, and other sources (labs/studies)
Document clinical reasoning by writing a brief assessment of the situation and a plan of care and admission orders for treatment and subsequent studies
PBLI: Individual learners write a brief (1-2 paragraphs) assessment of the case with instructions to provide reasons for their decisions, alternative diagnoses they considered and reasons that they settled on the diagnosis.
